newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares dip 2.6 pct at end of settlement.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares dip 2.6 pct at end of settlement.

text.p: Delhi shares closed sharply lower at the end of settlement amid disappointment the government did not offer more concessions to capital markets in a tax bill that cleared parliament this week, brokers said.
The Delhi bourse's benchmark index lost 19.39 points, or 2.6 percent, to close at 738.02.
"No major ammendments in the minimum alternate tax imposed on zero-tax companies gave an opportunity to bear operators to dominate the trading," said Sanjay Agarwal of brokers M.G. Associates.

This week Finance Minister P. Chidambaram made two, minor adjustments in the controversial minimum tax, disappointing financial markets which had been expecting the government to punch major loopholes in it.
Reliance Industries fell 6.65 rupees to 197 while TISCO closed 6.85 rupees lower at 177.
State Bank of India lost 14.65 rupees to close at 258. Oriental Bank of Commerce lost seven rupees at 75.
ITC ended 4.10 rupees down at 286 and Hindustan Lever quoted four rupees lower at 812.
ACC fell 89.95 rupees to close at 1,935.05.
